title: Cho-2021-revealing-10.1101/2021.02.12.430921
description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from eight human subjects performing a simple auditory reaction-time task, in which they pressed a button as quickly as possible after an auditory stimulus. The release contains downsampled (400 Hz) epochs locked to the stimulus and to the button press, plus 1-s rest segments, repackaged in iEEG-BIDS from the authors' Zenodo deposit. The data support analysis of the physiological origin of event-related potentials.
methods_description: ECoG was recorded with BCI2000 using g.USBamp or g.HIamp amplifiers at 1,200 Hz from subdural platinum-iridium grids (4 mm diameter, 10 mm spacing). Data were high-pass filtered at 0.05 Hz, common median referenced and downsampled to 400 Hz. They were then epoched around the auditory stimulus and the button press, with 1-s rest segments as baseline. Electrode locations were derived from postoperative radiographs/CT and MRI.
